US-based Lemkin Institute recognises 1971 genocide
2022-01-01T17:00:43+06:00 | Star Digital Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/us-based-lemkin-institute-recognises-1971-genocide-2930086

The Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention, an US-based institution, has recognised the brutal killings of Bangladeshis by the Pakistani occupation forces in 1971 as a 'genocide'.

Tawheed Reza Noor, son of martyred journalist Sirajuddin Hossain, applied for the recognition in mid-November last year.

The recognition was confirmed in an e-mailed statement from the Lemkin Institute last night, Tawheed Reza told The Daily Star.

He said it is probably the first official recognition of genocide in Bangladesh by an international research institute on genocide.

He further said, "I think this recognition of Lemkin Institute is an invaluable gift on the golden jubilee of the Liberation War of Bangladesh. This paved the way for the international recognition of genocide that took place in Bangladesh in 1971 and in the course of time many more organisations and countries will come forward to give recognition to the genocide."
